chunks: Ismaʿīl ibn Abī Ziyād narrated with his chain of transmission, saying:
The Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله said:

A riding animal has rights upon its owner: he begins by feeding it when he dismounts, offers it water when he passes by it, does not strike its face, for it glorifies its Lord with praise, does not remain standing upon its back except in the way of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, does not burden it beyond its capacity, and does not compel it in walking except to what it can bear.

key_terms.الْمَاءَ: water that should be offered to the animal when available
key_terms.الْمَشْيِ: walking or travel imposed upon the animal
key_terms.بِعَلْفِهَا: with its fodder, meaning feeding it properly
key_terms.تُسَبِّحُ: it glorifies Allah, indicating the creature’s praise of its Lord
key_terms.صَاحِبِهَا: its owner or keeper who is responsible for it
key_terms.طَاقَتِهَا: its capacity or ability, which must not be exceeded
key_terms.لِلدَّابَّةِ: the riding animal or beast that is owed care and consideration
key_terms.وَجْهَهَا: its face, which is forbidden to strike

ai.seo_question: What rights does a riding animal have over its owner in Islam?
ai.summary: This hadith teaches the rights of a riding animal over its owner and emphasizes mercy, restraint, and responsible treatment. It presents care for animals as part of moral conduct taught by the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله. The narration prohibits cruelty, overburdening, and needless hardship.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.2465 - Isma‘il ibn Abi Ziyad narrated with his chain of transmission that the Messenger of Allah (swt) (peace and blessings of Allah (swt) be upon him and his family) said:
"A mount has certain rights upon its owner:

-	Begin by feeding it when you dismount.
-	Offer it water when you pass by a source.
-	Do not strike its face, for it glorifies its Lord (azj) with praise.
-	Do not remain seated on its back except in the way of Allah (swt), the Mighty and Glorious.
-	Do not burden it beyond its capacity.
Do not compel it to walk more than it can endure."
